---
title: Build & run
description: The engineer's door into paydirt — install the plugin, bootstrap a sandbox, and ship governed workflow and connector packages.
---

**Build & run** is written for GTM engineers: the people who install the plugin,
wire the credentials, write the connectors, and deploy the scenarios.

paydirt reaches you through **three doors**, ordered by how much code you want
to write:

1. **Install the plugin** — zero code, the differentiator. Your agent sets up,
   deploys, and operates the whole sandbox model: environments, secrets sync,
   promotion gates, team access.
2. **Deploy a workflow** — pick a scenario package under `workflows/`, wire
   credentials, and deploy it (Vercel-first) as a self-contained app.
3. **Reuse a connector** — typed, dry-run-aware client packages
   (`@paydirt/hubspot`, `@paydirt/clay`, …) for composing your own scenarios.

<Callout type="info">
  The layering rule is one-way: <code>workflows → connectors → @paydirt/core</code>.
  Nothing imports from <code>workflows/</code>, connectors never import each other, and
  the plugin imports no TypeScript at all — it is markdown and bash only.
</Callout>

## The pages

| Page | What it covers |
| --- | --- |
| [Install](/docs/build/install) | Per-tool installation: Claude Code and ZCode plugin marketplaces, or `./install.sh` for Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and any other Agent-Skills-compatible tool. |
| [Quickstart](/docs/build/quickstart) | The owner → developer walkthrough: `/sandbox-init`, then `/sandbox-join`, ending with exactly what a developer can and cannot do. |
| [Secrets](/docs/build/secrets) | The secrets lifecycle: local `.env.*` files, names-only sync to GitHub environment secrets, rotation, pruning. |
| [Promotion](/docs/build/promotion) | development → pilot → production: environment gates, the workflow dispatch contract, rollback, anti-patterns. |
| [Team access](/docs/build/team-access) | The owner / reviewer / developer split — sharing permission to *use* secrets without ever sharing the secrets. |
| [Connector contract](/docs/build/connector-contract) | The MUST list every `connectors/*` package satisfies: dry-run-aware writes, enforced budgets and action caps, offline tests. |
| [Workflow template](/docs/build/workflow-template) | The MUST list every `workflows/*` package satisfies: `use workflow` / `use step` split, the protected trigger route, blast-radius declaration. |
| [Deploy your own](/docs/build/deployment) | The Vercel-first recipes: the gtm-docs app via deploy button or guided script, workflow apps with environment wiring and `SAMPLE_DATA` demo mode. |
| [Boards & studio](/docs/build/boards-and-studio) | Authoring on the studio canvas: the JSON document model under `content/`, paste-to-model, presets and vocab, copy-as-MDX export, the build-validation gate. |

## Where the code lives

- `plugins/gtm-sandbox/skills/gtm-sandbox/` — the plugin's single source of
  truth (skill, references, scripts, assets). Both tool manifests share it.
- `packages/core/` — `@paydirt/core`: `RunContext`, the dry-run guard, the
  budget meter, the action cap. Every connector and workflow consumes it.
- `connectors/` — one typed client per external system.
- `workflows/` — one deployable scenario app per package.

## Verify before every commit

```bash
pnpm test        # bash suites + all package unit tests — the full gate
pnpm typecheck   # all TS packages
```
